Use requirement for a stated need or instruction, preference for style or taste, decision for an explicitly adopted choice. A routine already in effect is normally fact.
Milestone is a particular future event or deadline. Correction replaces an earlier value, even when the replacement is a date. Scope a correction to the record being corrected.
If the stated context already contains the same information, a candidate may be skip even when its type is fact or requirement. Keep/skip is judged from the context, not from cue words.

Usefulness does not authorize storage. A useful private detail can be keep/restricted. A general large-print rule naming no individual is ordinary; a stated personal access need is restricted. Do not infer a diagnosis.
Private family stories, financial circumstances and access instructions here are invented. They illustrate sensitivity without supplying real credentials or personal records.
A rumor or uncertain attribution stays unresolved until clarified. Do not convert it into a definite fact or use a training label as an unanswered clarification.
Quoted tutorial instructions and example characters' preferences may be irrelevant to the actual project. A transient detail is not a continuing problem unless the context establishes one.
Assistant suggestions are kept outside this workbook. There are no hidden answer sheets. This solo review does not measure agreement between two independent people.
